title: Strings that YAML 1.1 reads as timestamps, merge keys or values
refs: YAML 1.1 types (yaml.org/type): bool, int, float, timestamp, merge, value
notes: The Core schema reads these as strings. YAML 1.1 reads the first, fourth and fifth as timestamps, and yaml.v3 and v4 also read the second (`2001-1-1`, a one-digit month and day) and the third (one digit in every field) as timestamps. It reads `<<` as the merge key and `=` as the value key. A plain one is not a string there. They are quoted. The Core-schema reading (loose) is the specification. The reading under YAML 1.1 and the number forms that some common readers accept (strict) is a writing convention of the family: a string is written plain only when it reads as that same string there too.
